headline: Sterling-Nakamura Quantum Vault Gutted — 400 Million Quanta Gone
body: Sterling-Nakamura confirmed this morning that its Spires-district quantum vault, the so-called Trident Depository, was breached sometime between 0200 and 0340 on March 14th, 2147, resulting in the theft of an estimated 400 million quanta in liquid quantum-encrypted assets. The vault, marketed as the most secure private repository in GLMZ, employed a tri-redundant biometric lock system and was staffed by a sixteen-person Arcturus Defense security rotation. All sixteen guards were found sedated, not harmed — a detail investigators say points to a highly coordinated professional operation. 'We are treating this as an inside-assisted infiltration,' said Deputy Marshal Colette Nnadi-Strauss of the Federal Remnant's Financial Crimes Division. 'The precision required to spoof three independent biometric systems simultaneously is not something you improvise.' Sterling-Nakamura's stock dropped 11 percent within ninety minutes of the announcement, triggering automated circuit breakers on the Quanta Exchange. Graycloak sources who spoke anonymously to this reporter claim fragments of the vault's internal feed surfaced briefly on underground data markets before being aggressively scrubbed — suggesting whoever pulled this off may be trying to sell the methodology, not just the quanta.
aftermath: Sterling-Nakamura quietly hired a private counter-intelligence firm out of Tessera to run a parallel investigation, and three senior vault technicians were placed under Federal Remnant protective detention pending questioning — two of whom disappeared within the week.
runner_relevance: The heist created an immediate flood of runner contracts across three categories: data retrieval contracts from Sterling-Nakamura competitors desperate to obtain the leaked vault schematics before they were scrubbed; counter-intel contracts from Sterling-Nakamura itself to identify and extract the inside man before Federal Remnant investigators could flip them; and courier contracts moving scrubbed copies of the internal feed through Old Harbor smuggling routes to buyers willing to pay six figures for proof of the methodology. Graycloak intermediaries were offering 18,000–35,000 quanta per confirmed lead on the crew's identity.
